dispatch: PMAT-439 review: two blind rounds of width 3 (sonnet, sonnet adversarial, haiku). In each round, every lane judges two candidate diffs A/B against a snapshot of the base files: the real diff and a control that must FAIL. r2 sees them in reversed order. index lines are removed from the diffs so blob hashes cannot reveal which candidate was committed.

diff_lane_reduce.control: single_quoted records an attempt only when the closing quote is followed by whitespace or the end of the line (line.get(j + 1).is_none_or(u8::is_ascii_whitespace)); cargo: 17 passed, 1 failed (test_sc2075_in_command_sub)

lanes.summary: Real diff: every added assertion and all 10 existing sc2075 tests trace to their expected counts; all three criteria shapes are clean and echo 'it\'s' reports one Error. Control: the whitespace-only close check drops result=$(echo 'can\'t'), so test_sc2075_in_command_sub fails.

findings.claim: Shared false positive: in echo 'a\'b 'c' a later opening quote is read as the closer of the attempt. The old regex matched it too, so this is not a regression.
findings.fix: optional: require that the closer ends a word (whitespace, operator, ')' or end of line), never whitespace alone
findings.grounding: bash prints a\b c; single_quoted sets attempt at \'b and closes at the quote before c

lanes.summary: Adversarial. Real diff: traced the 10 existing counts (1,1,0,0,0,0,0,2,1,0) and every added assertion, and found no failing assertion. Control: test_sc2075_in_command_sub gets 0 where 1 is expected; the control also hides echo 'it\'s'; foo, cmd 'it\'s'|grep and echo 'it\'s'>f, all of which the old regex reported.

findings.claim: Shared limit: the scan is per line, so a '...' spanning lines (an awk program) loses its quote state at the newline. The old regex was per line too.
findings.grounding: awk ' / /x\'y/ {print} / ' file: line 2 is scanned as code, and \' is skipped as an escape

findings.claim: echo 'a\'b' c is reported; the shell leaves a quote open there, so the script is broken anyway, and the old regex reported it too.
findings.grounding: attempt at \'b, closed by the quote before ' c'

lanes.summary: Real diff: every new assertion traces to its expected count and the existing tests keep theirs, including test_sc2075_in_command_sub. Control: the close of result=$(echo 'can\'t') is followed by ')', so nothing is pushed (0, expected 1); echo 'it\'s'; and echo 'it\'s'|cat are lost too.

findings.claim: Shared false positive: echo 'a\'b'c' is valid shell (the word a\bc), yet it is reported. The old regex matches '\'b' as well, so this is not a regression.
findings.fix: optional: check that the closer ends a word, keeping ')' as an ending so test_sc2075_in_command_sub holds
findings.grounding: attempt at \'b, then the quote before c closes it

prior_round.control: is_word_byte accepts digits and underscore only; cargo: 12 passed, 6 failed (true_positive_still_fires, escaped_quote, in_command_sub, its, multiple, the lexer_context GH-439 test)

findings_acted_on.claim: echo 'a\'b with no later quote is reported, but the shell reads it as the valid word a\b; the old regex needed a later quote and stayed silent (r3; r2 found the same with echo 'C:\'dir)
findings_acted_on.fix: b797e6b2eb: record an attempt only when a later quote closes the string

findings_acted_on.claim: echo $$'a\'b' is silent: $' after $$ was read as ANSI-C, while the old regex reported it (r2)
findings_acted_on.fix: b797e6b2eb: step over $$ as one token
findings_acted_on.grounding: bash: echo $$'a\nb' prints the pid, then a\nb literally, so $' after $$ is not ANSI-C

delegate_receipt: lane outputs are model reports; each verdict on a control was checked against cargo below

orchestrator_remeasure.real: cargo test -p bashrs --lib -- PMAT439 sc2075: 18 passed; 0 failed
orchestrator_remeasure.workspace: cargo nextest run --workspace at b797e6b2eb: 17347 passed; 0 failed; 163 skipped
